stories.headline: UAE exits OPEC and OPEC+ effective May 1, triggering global reaction and deepening UAE-Saudi rift
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced on April 28 it would leave OPEC and the broader OPEC+ alliance effective May 1, stripping the cartel of its third-largest producer. The decision — announced the same day as an emergency GCC summit in Jeddah where the UAE sent only its foreign minister rather than MBZ — was framed officially as an assertion of national energy sovereignty but was widely analyzed as the culmination of years of friction with Saudi Arabia over production quotas, regional strategy, and MBZ-MBS personal rivalry. Trump welcomed the move; OPEC+ (now without UAE) held its first post-exit meeting on May 3 and agreed a symbolic 188,000 bpd production hike. A UAE official confirmed the country was reviewing but not planning further withdrawals from multilateral organizations.

stories.headline: ADNOC announces $55 billion project awards for 2026–2028 and major US natural gas expansion push
stories.summary: ADNOC announced on May 3 at its 'Make it with ADNOC' forum that it will award AED 200 billion ($55 billion) in project contracts between 2026 and 2028, accelerating its five-year capex plan post-OPEC exit and emphasizing UAE local manufacturing. Separately, it had been reported earlier in the week that ADNOC's international arm XRG is evaluating 29 potential deals to build a vertically integrated US natural gas business worth tens of billions of dollars, targeting LNG exports and data center demand. CEO Sultan Al Jaber described both moves as entering a 'new phase of growth.'
